h1: SEO in Chennai, in Tamil and English both
metaTitle: SEO Company in Chennai: Tamil and English Keywords
metaDescription: A real share of Chennai search happens in Tamil and Tanglish. We build both keyword sets for auto, healthcare and IT firms, on a 90-day guarantee.
answer: Chennai is the Indian metro where a bilingual keyword set changes the result most. Tamil-script and Tanglish queries carry real commercial intent for clinics, retail and local services, while auto-component exporters and OMR software firms sell almost entirely in English. We build both sets from day one, on a 90-day baseline guarantee.
takeaways: Tamil keyword work is the **first deliverable** on a Chennai consumer account, not a line item added in month five.
Most Tamil search arrives as **Tanglish** — Tamil words typed in Roman script. Translating your site into Tamil script and stopping there misses the larger half.
Oragadam and Sriperumbudur exporters need part numbers, standards and certifications indexed. Their buyers never type a Tamil word.
Chennai's medical map pack is fought **neighbourhood by neighbourhood** — Adyar, Anna Nagar, Velachery, Porur, Tambaram are five separate contests.
Voice queries are longer and question-shaped. That's a phrasing change, not a separate channel.

sections.h2: Three languages, one site, and the one most agencies skip
body: Chennai search doesn't split neatly into Tamil and English. It splits three ways, and the middle one is where the volume actually sits.

Tamil script — proper Tamil typed in Tamil characters — is used, mostly by older searchers and mostly for news, government and entertainment queries. English is the default for anything professional. Between them sits Tanglish: Tamil words typed in Roman letters, which is what most people's phone keyboards produce with no effort. "Pallam", "maruthuvamanai", "veedu vaadagai", "kadai" — all of it shows up in Latin characters in real query data.

The failure mode we see constantly: an agency translates ten pages into Tamil script, ticks the box, and captures almost nothing, because the searchers they were aiming at type in Roman letters. The correct order of work is the opposite.
numbered: **Export twelve months of Search Console queries** and sort for non-English words in Roman script. This is free, it's your own data, and it tells you which Tanglish phrasings already land on you.
**Fold those phrasings into existing English pages** — in headings, in FAQ answers, in the way you name things. A page can rank for both languages when it contains both.
**Only then consider Tamil-script pages**, and only for the intents where a genuinely Tamil-first audience buys: clinics, coaching, retail, home services, government-adjacent processes.
**Never machine-translate and walk away.** Tamil has enough register and dialect variation that a bad translation reads as spam to a human and converts like it too.

callout.title: When a second language version earns its keep
callout.body: A Tamil-script section doubles your content maintenance forever. It's worth it when the audience is mass-market consumer and the pages are evergreen. It's usually not worth it for B2B. We work through that decision in [English vs regional-language SEO](/compare/english-vs-regional-language-seo).

sections.h2: Oragadam and Sriperumbudur: the buyer is in Stuttgart
body: Chennai has a fair claim to being India's automotive capital. Hyundai at Irungattukottai, Renault-Nissan and Daimler's commercial vehicle plant at Oragadam, Royal Enfield, Ashok Leyland at Ennore, TVS, and the enormous component belt around Ambattur, Sriperumbudur and Maraimalai Nagar. Foxconn, Samsung and Salcomp anchor the electronics side.

If you're a tier-2 or tier-3 supplier in that belt, your search problem has nothing to do with Chennai and everything to do with procurement engineers in Germany, Japan and the American Midwest. They search the way engineers search: precisely, and never in marketing language.
That means the pages that win are specification pages, not "About Us" pages. Concretely, the things worth having indexed are:
bullets: **Process plus material plus capability** — aluminium high-pressure die casting, hot forging up to 25 kg, CNC machining tolerance ±0.01 mm.

**Standards and certifications** — IATF 16949, ISO 14001, PPAP level 3, APQP, ISO 9001. These are filter terms in a buyer's shortlist, and they belong in indexable text, not inside a PDF or a JPEG of a certificate.
**Part families and application** — brake components, EV battery enclosures, transmission housings, wiring harness connectors.
**Capacity and commercial terms** — minimum order quantity, tooling lead time, export documentation, Incoterms you actually trade on.
**Country-shaped queries** — India-based supplier, China plus one alternative, second-source manufacturer.

callout.title: The PDF problem
callout.body: Half the export sites we audit in this belt keep every specification inside a downloadable catalogue PDF. Google can index PDFs, but they rank poorly, convert worse, and can't be internally linked into a topic cluster. Rebuild the catalogue as HTML pages and keep the PDF as the download. It's frequently the single biggest win on an [exporter's site](/seo-for/exporters).

sections.h2: Hospitals and diagnostics: five neighbourhoods, five contests
body: Chennai is one of India's largest medical-treatment destinations, drawing patients from across South India, the North East, and abroad. It's also a city where healthcare demand is intensely local: nobody crosses Chennai in traffic for a routine scan.

Which means "diagnostic centre in Chennai" is close to a vanity keyword, and "blood test near Anna Nagar" is the one that fills a slot. The map pack resolves by proximity, so a single-location clinic in Adyar and a single-location clinic in Tambaram are not competitors — they're running two entirely separate races, and a chain is running one race per branch.

The work follows from that. Each branch needs its own Google Business Profile, its own landing page with a real address and real photos, its own review flow, and enough distinct on-page content that the branch pages aren't near-duplicates of each other. Doing this properly is most of what [local SEO services](/services/local-seo-services) actually consists of.

One warning specific to healthcare in India: claim language is regulated. The Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act restricts what you can say about treating specific conditions, and Google's own quality guidelines hold health pages to a higher evidence bar than almost anything else. Named, credentialled doctors on the page, with registration numbers, beats adjectives every time.

sections.h2: OMR: Chennai's software belt sells everywhere except Chennai
body: The Rajiv Gandhi Salai corridor — OMR, out through Perungudi, Thoraipakkam, Sholinganallur and SIPCOT Siruseri — is where Chennai's product and services software sits. Zoho and Freshworks both grew out of this city, which has quietly made Chennai one of India's most credible SaaS towns.

For those companies, Chennai is an office address and nothing more. A buyer evaluating helpdesk software in Manchester does not filter by your registered office. So none of the local tactics on this page apply, and pretending otherwise would be an easy way to sell you a package you don't need.

What does apply: bottom-of-funnel pages built around comparison and integration intent, documentation that ranks, pricing pages that are actually crawlable, and a link profile earned from real technical publications rather than paid placements. Slower, and the only version that survives a core update.

Chennai gets brought up in voice-search conversations a lot, usually with a confident-sounding percentage attached. We won't give you one, because there is no credible published figure for voice query share in a single Indian city, and quoting a made-up one would be the fastest way to lose your trust.

What we can say is mechanical and useful. A spoken query is longer than a typed one and shaped like a full sentence. "Dentist Velachery" becomes "which dentist near Velachery is open now on Sunday". Spoken Tamil transcribes into a mix of Tamil and English words that no keyword tool will show you a volume for.

So the practical response isn't a "voice SEO strategy". It's writing pages that answer complete questions in complete sentences, keeping opening hours and service areas accurate in your Business Profile, and mining your own Search Console for the long question-shaped queries you already receive. That covers the majority of it at roughly zero incremental cost.

callout.title: Where the long tail lives
callout.body: Question-shaped queries are individually tiny and collectively enormous. We don't drop a keyword because a tool reports its volume as zero — on long-tail phrasings the tools are guessing, and your own Search Console isn't.

body: We take three clients a month across every city we work in. That's the constraint that makes the guarantee affordable to us — you can't carry downside risk at volume.

Pricing is the same in Chennai as everywhere else, because the work is the same: **SEO from ₹75,000/mo, smaller sites from ₹40,000/mo**, ex-GST. Bilingual keyword research is included at both tiers. Tamil-script content production, if you decide you need it, is quoted separately because it's a genuine extra cost and we'd rather show it than bury it.

If we haven't beaten that number in 90 days, we keep working free until we do. faqs.q: Do I need my website in Tamil to rank in Chennai?
faqs.a: Usually not the whole site. Most Tamil-language search in Chennai arrives as Tanglish — Tamil words typed in Roman script — which a well-written English page can rank for if those phrasings appear naturally in the copy. Full Tamil-script pages earn their maintenance cost for consumer categories like clinics, coaching and retail.

faqs.q: What does an SEO company in Chennai charge?
faqs.a: Our SEO starts at ₹75,000/mo, smaller sites from ₹40,000/mo, ex-GST. Across the wider Chennai market quotes run from a few thousand rupees a month upward. Below roughly ₹25,000/mo you're funding part-time freelance attention, which is fine for one local outlet and useless for an export or SaaS keyword set.

faqs.q: Can SEO help an auto-component exporter in Oragadam or Sriperumbudur?
faqs.a: Yes, and it's often underused. Procurement engineers search processes, tolerances, part families and certifications like IATF 16949. Most supplier sites hide all of that inside a catalogue PDF where it ranks badly. Converting the catalogue into indexable HTML pages is frequently the largest single win available.

faqs.q: How long does SEO take to show results in Chennai?
faqs.a: For a single-location clinic, retailer or service business, four to eight weeks to visible movement, mostly from Business Profile and local work. For export B2B or SaaS competing internationally, three to six months minimum, and often longer from a standing start. We tell you which one you are before you sign, not after.

faqs.q: Do you handle multiple hospital or clinic branches across Chennai?
faqs.a: Yes. Each branch gets its own Business Profile, its own landing page with a genuine address, its own review flow and enough distinct content that the branch pages aren't near-duplicates. Adyar, Anna Nagar, Velachery, Porur and Tambaram are five separate map-pack contests, not one.

faqs.q: Do you guarantee a number one ranking in Chennai?
faqs.a: No. Nobody controls Google's index, and Google's own guidelines warn against position guarantees. What we guarantee is movement against your own frozen baseline: your trailing-90-day qualified leads from organic search. Miss it in 90 days and we keep working free until we beat it.
